title.narrative: Adequate Housing for All - UN-Habitat's knowledge hub on inclusive, sustainable and adequate housing at the centre of sustainable development

description.narrative: The shift towards a mostly urban world makes the process of urbanization one of the most significant global trends of the 21st century. Compounded by rapid population growth and persistent levels of poverty, governments and cities are struggling to meet housing needs. Around 1.6 billion people globally live in inadequate housing conditions, without access to basic services or sanitation, struggling to afford housing costs or facing threats of eviction. The COVID-19 pandemic has shed light on and exacerbated this pre-existing housing crisis. At the same time, the health, social and economic crisis brought on by COVID-19 has highlighted the key role of housing in both preventing, building resilience to and recovering from systemic shocks. The pandemic exposed structural social and economic inequalities and vast gaps in the social protection system that demand a new social contract. “Our Common Agenda”, which was resented by the Secretary-General calls for a renewed social contract between Governments and people and within societies, to rebuild trust and embrace a comprehensive vision of human rights. Among the four core elements of the new social contract, there is the right to adequate housing for all and the call for governments to respect, protect and fulfil this fundamental right. The sustainable future of cities and the enjoyment of adequate standards of living for all strongly depend on facing and tackling housing challenges worldwide. Trends include an ageing population, the spreading of online platforms for short-term rentals, changing preferences and use following the shift to remote working for certain categories of the population, the need to reduce the carbon footprint of constructions and improve the energy efficiency of the existing building stock, are increasingly calling for rethinking of current systems and to strengthen coordinated actions between actors. UN-Habitat is the coordinating agency within the UN system for promoting collaboration on the implementation of SDG 11 and its target 11.1, as well as the realisation of the NUA, of the right to adequate housing enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, aims at facilitating partnerships and collaborations in the housing sector by bridging gaps in knowledge, strengthening capacities, testing innovative approaches on the ground, and giving visibility to partner's efforts. Through the project, in particular, UN-Habitat will aim to increase knowledge development, exchange and joint advocacy among stakeholders in the housing sector through the creation of a Knowledge Hub on Housing.
